claim: This video shows real people collecting floating iPhone boxes after a ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz.
caption:
FALSE: This specific video of people collecting floating iPhone boxes in the Strait of Hormuz is AI-generated, according to Full Fact. Its 27 October check reports a SynthID watermark and continuity errors, including a changing number of boxes. These are Full Fact’s findings; we did not run the detector or independently inspect the referenced Facebook post.

The sinking itself was real: Singapore’s Maritime and Port Authority confirmed that GFS PRIDE sank and its crew were safely evacuated. This video check does not establish what cargo was aboard or deny other real cargo-recovery footage. It does not identify who caused the sinking.

AI illustration — not actual footage. The accompanying artwork is an original generic illustration, not a video frame or evidence of the event.

Sources:
https://fullfact.org/world/video-people-collecting-iPhones-Strait-Hormuz-ai-generated/
https://leadstories.com/hoax-alert/2026/10/fact-check-fake-video-shows-people-fishing-iphones-out-of-water-after-missile-attack-on-ship-in-strait-of-hormuz-it-is-ai.html
https://www.mpa.gov.sg/media-centre/details/two-singapore-registered-vessels-struck-in-strait-of-hormuz

Checked 28 October 2026. AI-assisted research, design and original illustration; independent automated evidence/editorial review.
evidence_summary: Full Fact reports SynthID and continuity evidence identifying this specific video as AI-generated. Lead Stories documents circulation. MPA confirms the real GFS PRIDE sinking. No independent detector run, cargo conclusion or attribution of responsibility is claimed.
claim_date_note: Lead Stories publication establishes circulation by October20. Its October17 social-post date is secondary reporting, not the date or origin of the referenced unavailable Facebook post.

visual_provenance.generation_prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: original editorial illustration for a fact-check card, not evidence and not a reconstruction of real footage. Primary request: an obviously hand-made nonphotographic illustration of an abstract sea and a single closed, unbranded shipping box floating at the surface. Scene/backdrop: simplified layered ocean wave shapes, with generous uncluttered negative space; no identifiable location. Subject: exactly one plain closed cardboard shipping box, no markings or visible contents. Style/medium: bold editorial paper-cut collage with softly textured gouache, visibly stylized flat shapes, not 3D photorealism or camera footage. Composition/framing: landscape 3:2 composition, box near the lower center, calm graphic rhythm and clear silhouette readable at small card size. Constraints: no text, lettering, logos, watermark, labels, phones, phone packaging, people, hands, ships, boats, wreckage, coastline landmarks, or documentary visual cues. Do not imitate any existing viral footage. The art must be a generic symbolic illustration, not a realistic depiction of an event.
